days.title: Types of Pilgrimage Rites, the Miqats and the Prohibitions of Ihram
days.question: What is the difference between ifrad, qiran and tamattu'? And what is forbidden for someone in ihram?
days.principle: The rites are three: ifrad, qiran and tamattu'. The Prophet ﷺ set the places for entering ihram (the miqats), and a man in ihram must avoid sewn clothing, covering the head, shaving hair, clipping nails, touching perfume and killing land game.

misconception.peopleSay: Anyone in ihram who does something prohibited must pay a ransom, even if he forgot.
misconception.correct: If he does something prohibited in ihram out of forgetfulness or ignorance, nothing is due from him; if he does it deliberately, a ransom is due: fasting, charity or a sacrifice.

days.action: Write down the four miqats and the regions they serve, and find out which miqat would be yours if you travelled for Hajj or 'Umrah from your country.
lesson: Aisha related that in the Farewell Hajj some of them entered ihram for 'Umrah, some for Hajj and 'Umrah together, and some for Hajj only. The Prophet ﷺ commanded the Companions who had not brought sacrificial animals to leave ihram after tawaf and sa'y, shorten their hair and make it tamattu', and said that had he not brought the sacrificial animal he would have done as they did. The Prophet ﷺ set miqats for ihram: Dhul-Hulayfah for the people of Madinah, al-Juhfah for the people of Sham, Qarn al-Manazil for the people of Najd and Yalamlam for the people of Yemen, and 'Umar set Dhat 'Irq for the people of Iraq. A man in ihram avoids sewn clothing, covering the head, shaving hair, cutting nails, perfume and hunting land game. If he does any of these out of forgetfulness or ignorance, nothing is due from him; if deliberately, a ransom is due: fasting three days, feeding six poor people or slaughtering a sheep.

quiz.question: Someone in ihram forgot and wore a sewn garment. What is due from him?
quiz.explanation: If he does any of that out of forgetfulness or ignorance, nothing is due from him.

quiz.question: Someone is coming from Sham for Hajj. Where does he enter ihram?
options: From al-Juhfah, the miqat the Prophet ﷺ set

quiz.question: If your route does not pass through any of the miqats, where do you enter ihram?
options: From the point parallel to one

askTheBook: How did the Companions enter ihram in the Farewell Hajj?
What are the miqats of ihram?

days.title: Step by Step: How to Perform Hajj
days.question: What does the pilgrim do, in order, from ihram until the Day of Sacrifice?
days.principle: The pilgrim prepares for ihram by bathing, cleaning himself, applying perfume and removing sewn clothing; then he enters ihram on reaching the miqat and says the talbiyah, performs tawaf and sa'y, goes out to Mina on the eighth day, stands at 'Arafah, moves on to Muzdalifah, and then on the Day of Sacrifice throws pebbles at Jamrat al-'Aqabah, sacrifices and shaves his head.

misconception.peopleSay: If a pilgrim does the rites of the Day of Sacrifice out of order, his Hajj has a big problem.
misconception.correct: Whatever is done earlier or later among the rites of the Day of Sacrifice, whether throwing, shaving, sacrificing or tawaf, there is no harm.

days.action: Memorise the supplication said between the two corners during tawaf: «اللهم آتنا في الدنيا حسنة وفي الآخرة حسنة وقنا عذاب النار», and supplicate with it today.
lesson: The pilgrim prepares for ihram by bathing, cleaning himself and applying perfume, and wears a lower wrap, an upper wrap and sandals when he reaches the miqat, raising his voice with the talbiyah. When he reaches the House he performs seven circuits of tawaf starting from the Black Stone with the House on his left, walking briskly (raml) in the first three circuits of the arrival tawaf, and prays two units behind the Station of Ibrahim if possible. Then he performs sa'y between Safa and Marwah, seven times, starting at Safa and ending at Marwah. On the eighth day he goes to Mina, and on the day of 'Arafah he stands at 'Arafah until sunset, then moves on to Muzdalifah and spends the night there. On the Day of Sacrifice he throws seven pebbles at Jamrat al-'Aqabah, sacrifices his animal if performing tamattu' or qiran, and shaves or shortens his hair; a woman shortens hers by a fingertip's length. And if he does any of the rites of the Day of Sacrifice earlier or later, there is no harm.
days.quote: All of 'Arafah is a place of standing except the valley of 'Uranah, and the time of standing there is from the sun passing its zenith on the day of 'Arafah until dawn on the Day of Sacrifice.

quiz.question: On the Day of Sacrifice a pilgrim shaved before throwing the pebbles. Is anything due from him?
quiz.explanation: Whatever is done earlier or later among the rites of the Day of Sacrifice, whether throwing, shaving, sacrificing or tawaf, there is no harm.

quiz.question: A pilgrim reached 'Arafah at night, after Maghrib and before Fajr. Is his standing valid?
options: No, it must be before Maghrib
No, he has missed the Hajj
Valid but he owes a ransom
Yes, the time of standing lasts until dawn on the Day of Sacrifice
quiz.explanation: The time of standing there is from the sun passing its zenith on the day of 'Arafah until dawn on the Day of Sacrifice.

quiz.question: What does raml in tawaf mean?
quiz.explanation: Raml is walking briskly with short steps.

askTheBook: What are the steps of Hajj in order?
How are tawaf and sa'y performed?
What are the rites of the Day of Sacrifice?

days.title: The Days of Tashriq and the Farewell, and the Beginning of the Prophet's ﷺ Hajj
days.question: What does the pilgrim do after the Day of Sacrifice? And how did the Prophet ﷺ perform Hajj?
days.principle: The pilgrim throws the pebbles at the jamarat on the days of tashriq, each day after midday, and does not leave Makkah until he performs the farewell tawaf so that his last contact is with the House, except a menstruating woman, who is permitted to leave it. Jabir narrated the description of the Prophet's ﷺ Hajj.

misconception.peopleSay: Visiting the Prophet's Mosque is one of the rites of Hajj, and whoever doesn't visit it has a deficient Hajj.
misconception.correct: After finishing the rites of Hajj it is recommended to visit the Mosque of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ to pray in it and then greet him, but visiting the Prophet's Mosque is not counted among the rites of Hajj.

days.action: Memorise the Prophet's ﷺ talbiyah «لبيك اللهم لبيك، لبيك لا شريك لك لبيك...» and think about its meaning: that you are answering Allah's call and bearing witness that He has no partner.
lesson: After the Day of Sacrifice the pilgrim returns to Mina and spends two nights there if he hurries, or three if he stays, throwing at the three jamarat each day after midday. Whoever misses throwing on one day throws the next day, and weak women and elderly people can appoint someone to throw for them. The pilgrim may not leave Makkah before the farewell tawaf, except a menstruating woman, who is permitted to. After Hajj it is recommended to visit the Prophet's Mosque and greet the Prophet ﷺ, but it is not one of the rites of Hajj. Then the book relates the Prophet's ﷺ Hajj as Jabir narrated it: he entered ihram with tawhid in the famous talbiyah, performed tawaf walking briskly for three circuits and walking for four, and prayed behind the Station. On Safa he declared Allah's oneness, magnified Him and supplicated, and said: I begin with what Allah began with.
days.quote: Visiting the Prophet's Mosque is not counted among the rites of Hajj.

quiz.question: A woman pilgrim's period started before the farewell tawaf. What does she do?
options: Travel without it; she has a concession
quiz.explanation: No one is exempt from that except the menstruating woman, who is permitted to leave it.

quiz.question: You missed throwing on one of the days of tashriq. What do you do?
quiz.explanation: Whoever misses throwing on one day throws it the next day, because all the days of tashriq are a time for throwing.

quiz.question: Is visiting the Prophet's Mosque one of the rites of Hajj?
options: Hajj is not valid without it
No, it is recommended but not one of the rites
quiz.explanation: Visiting the Prophet's Mosque is not counted among the rites of Hajj.

askTheBook: What does the pilgrim do on the days of tashriq?
What is the ruling on the farewell tawaf?
What was the Prophet's ﷺ talbiyah?

days.title: The Hajj of the Prophet ﷺ
days.question: How was the Prophet ﷺ at 'Arafah, Muzdalifah and Mina?
days.principle: In his Hajj ﷺ he prayed at Mina on the day of Tarwiyah, then stood at 'Arafah until the sun set, then moved on to Muzdalifah calmly and prayed Maghrib and 'Isha' there, then stood at al-Mash'ar al-Haram until it was very bright, then threw at the jamrah, sacrificed and went on to the House.

misconception.peopleSay: Leaving Muzdalifah must be after Fajr for everyone without exception.
misconception.correct: The Prophet ﷺ permitted the weak to leave Muzdalifah at night: «استأذنته سودة وكانت امرأة ضخمة ثبطة أن تفيض من جمع بليل فأذن لها».

days.action: When you are in a hurry or in a crowd today, remember the Prophet ﷺ telling the people during Hajj «السكينة السكينة», and try to walk calmly and deal gently.
lesson: The book continues the hadith of Jabir: on the day of Tarwiyah the Prophet ﷺ went to Mina and prayed Dhuhr, 'Asr, Maghrib, 'Isha' and Fajr there. Then he went to 'Arafah, addressed the people, prayed Dhuhr and 'Asr combined, and stood facing the qiblah until the sun set. He moved on to Muzdalifah pulling in his camel's reins and signalling to the people with his hand: calm, calm. In Muzdalifah he prayed Maghrib and 'Isha' with one adhan and two iqamahs, slept until Fajr, then stood at al-Mash'ar al-Haram supplicating and magnifying Allah until it became very bright. On the way, he turned al-Fadl's face away with his hand when he looked at the women passing by. Then he threw seven pebbles at the jamrah, sacrificed, and went on to the House. The Prophet ﷺ permitted the weak to leave Muzdalifah at night.

quiz.question: How did the Prophet ﷺ pray Maghrib and 'Isha' in Muzdalifah?
options: Each prayer in its own time
Combined, with one adhan and two iqamahs

quiz.question: Until when did the Prophet ﷺ remain at 'Arafah?
When al-Fadl looked at the women, what did the Prophet ﷺ do?
options: He turned his face away with his hand, teaching lowering the gaze

askTheBook: How did the Prophet ﷺ stand at 'Arafah?
What did the Prophet ﷺ do in Muzdalifah?
What is the concession for the weak to leave Muzdalifah?

days.title: Marriage: The Only Way to Build a Family
days.question: Why does Islam encourage marriage? And why is zina a major sin?
days.principle: Marriage is the only lawful way to build a Muslim family; relationships outside this framework are among the major sins that anger Allah and His Messenger. Allah has forbidden zina and whatever words or deeds lead to it.

misconception.peopleSay: True asceticism is staying away from marriage and devoting oneself to worship.
misconception.correct: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ forbade monasticism and withdrawing from women, and said to the group who wanted that: «لكني أصوم وأفطر، وأصلي وأرقد، وأتزوج النساء، فمن رغب عن سنتي فليس مني».

days.action: If you are a young man or know one who is not yet married, remember the Prophet's ﷺ advice «من استطاع فليتزوج ومن لم يستطع فعليه بالصوم», and think of one practical step that brings you closer to the halal.
lesson: The book begins the third chapter with a fundamental rule: marriage is the only lawful way to build a Muslim family. Allah made marriage one of His signs, with tranquillity, affection and mercy in it, and it is the way of the prophets and messengers. The Prophet ﷺ urged young people to marry because it better lowers the gaze and guards chastity, and whoever cannot should fast. When three men decided to give up marriage, sleep or eating in order to worship, he told them that he was the most God-fearing of them and he marries, and whoever turns away from his Sunnah is not of him. In contrast, Allah forbade zina and everything that comes near it, saying ﴿وَلَا تَقْرَبُواْ ٱلزِّنَىٰٓ﴾. The Prophet ﷺ said that faith is pulled away from the one committing zina at the time he commits it, and if he repents it returns to him.
days.quote: Allah has favoured His servants with what He legislated for them of marriage, and made it one of His signs.

quiz.question: A young man wants to marry but cannot afford it. What did the Prophet ﷺ direct him to?
options: Fasting, because it is a protection

quiz.question: Someone decided not to marry so he can devote himself to worship. Does that agree with the Sunnah?
options: No, the Prophet ﷺ said: whoever turns away from my Sunnah is not of me
It is the most complete way

quiz.question: What is the ruling on a relationship between a man and a woman outside marriage?
options: One of the major sins, and marriage is the only lawful way
Permissible if they will marry later
quiz.explanation: And that sexual relationships outside this framework are among the major sins that anger Allah and His Messenger.

askTheBook: Why is marriage important in Islam?
What did the Prophet ﷺ say to young people about marriage?
What did Islam forbid to block the way to zina?

days.title: Blocking the Means: Lowering the Gaze and Seclusion
days.question: Why does Islam command lowering the gaze and forbid seclusion? Isn't the intention what matters most?
days.principle: Just as Allah forbade zina, He cut off the means to it and forbade every word or deed that leads to it: He commanded lowering the gaze, forbade speaking in a soft, enticing manner, and forbade seclusion with a non-mahram woman and a woman travelling without a mahram.

misconception.peopleSay: The husband's relatives, like his brother and cousin, have nothing to do with seclusion; they're family.
misconception.correct: The Prophet ﷺ said «الحمو الموت». Al-hamw means the husband's relatives other than his father and sons. People have customarily been lax about this, so the Prophet ﷺ warned against it.

days.action: If your eyes suddenly fall on something not halal today, turn them away immediately, as the Prophet ﷺ commanded Jarir ibn 'Abdillah.
lesson: Islam did not stop at forbidding zina; it closed every door that could lead to it. It commanded men and women to lower their gaze and guard their chastity, and the Prophet ﷺ commanded Jarir to turn his gaze away from a sudden glance. The Prophet ﷺ called deliberately looking at a non-mahram woman without need the zina of the eye, and he refrained from shaking hands with women in the pledge of allegiance. He forbade speaking in a soft, enticing manner that would make someone with a disease in his heart covet, and forbade a woman from wearing perfume when going out so as to tempt people. He forbade seclusion with a non-mahram woman, warned against laxity with the husband's relatives and said al-hamw is death. He also forbade a woman from travelling without a mahram.
days.quote: The Prophet ﷺ refrained from shaking hands with women in the pledge of allegiance, even though the custom in pledges was to strike hands.

quiz.question: You looked at a non-mahram woman unintentionally. What do you do?
A woman sat alone at home with her husband's brother. What is the ruling?
options: Permissible if the door is open
quiz.explanation: What is meant by al-hamw is the husband's relatives other than his father and sons.

quiz.question: A man had signed up for a military expedition while his wife was going out for Hajj alone. What did the Prophet ﷺ tell him?
options: Go back and perform Hajj with your wife

days.title: Women Are the Counterparts of Men
days.question: How does Islam view women? And what are their rights as mothers and daughters?
days.principle: Women are the counterparts of men; Allah gave them rights similar to their obligations, in kindness. He honoured woman as a mother, daughter, wife and relative, lifted the injustices of the Jahiliyyah from her, and gave the man guardianship (qiwamah) that is one of care, provision and responsibility, not of oppression and domination.

misconception.peopleSay: Guardianship (qiwamah) means the man controls and dominates his wife however he wants.
misconception.correct: Allah gave guardianship in the Muslim home to the man, and it is a guardianship of care, provision and responsibility, not of oppression and domination; and He established the marital relationship on mercy, affection and mutual rights.

days.action: Do something special for your mother today (a call, a visit, a gift or some help), and remember that the Prophet ﷺ said "your mother" three times before "your father".
lesson: The book establishes that women are the counterparts of men, with rights similar to their obligations, in kindness. Islam honoured woman as a mother, making her right to kindness three times that of the father, because she alone bore the pregnancy, birth and nursing. It commanded kindness to her even if she is a polytheist, and forbade undutifulness to her, making it a major sin. It honoured her as a daughter: the Prophet ﷺ said whoever raises two daughters until they reach maturity will come on the Day of Resurrection with him like two fingers of a hand. It made her the one who decides on her marriage, and when a father married off his daughter against her wishes, the Prophet ﷺ annulled the marriage. It honoured her as a wife; the Prophet ﷺ said: treat women well, and the best of you are the best to their families.
days.quote: That is because the mother alone bore the pregnancy, birth and nursing, and shared with the father in raising the child, so it was fitting that her right be multiplied three times over his.

quiz.question: Mother and father: whose right to kindness is greater?
options: The mother; her right is multiplied three times
quiz.explanation: That is because the mother alone bore the pregnancy, birth and nursing, and shared with the father in raising the child.

quiz.question: Someone's non-Muslim mother is coming to visit him. What does he do?
options: Maintain ties with her and treat her kindly

quiz.question: A father married off his daughter without her consent. What did the Prophet ﷺ do in such a case?
options: He told her to be patient

days.title: Lifting the Injustices of the Jahiliyyah, and Engagement and the Marriage Contract
days.question: What was the situation of women before Islam? And how are engagement and the contract done in Islam?
days.principle: Engagement is a promise of marriage, in which each of the engaged should see the other without seclusion; a man may not propose to a woman someone else has already proposed to. The marriage contract is offer and acceptance, and it requires a guardian and two witnesses, with a well-known disagreement about the guardian.

misconception.peopleSay: A woman has no inheritance; money is for the adult men only.
misconception.correct: In the Jahiliyyah the polytheists gave wealth to the adult men and did not let women or children inherit, so Allah revealed: «للرجال نصيب مما ترك الوالدان والأقربون وللنساء نصيب». So all are equal in the principle of inheritance.

days.action: If you or someone you know is choosing a spouse, remember the Prophetic advice «فاظفر بذات الدين», and make religion the first criterion.
lesson: The book continues with how Islam lifted the injustices of the Jahiliyyah from women: a woman was inherited like property, had no share in inheritance, and a man would divorce her and take her back a hundred times to harm her. The Quran came down forbidding inheriting women against their will, giving women a share of inheritance, and limiting divorce to twice. 'Umar said that in the Jahiliyyah they did not regard women as anything until Allah revealed what He revealed about them. Then the book talks about engagement: it is a promise of marriage, and it is recommended that each see the other without seclusion; the Prophet ﷺ told al-Mughirah to look at her, for it is more likely to create lasting affection between them. A man may not propose to a woman his brother has already proposed to. The Prophet ﷺ advised choosing a religious woman, and the marriage contract is offer and acceptance with a guardian and two witnesses, with a well-known disagreement about the guardian.
days.quote: Meaning: all are equal in it in Allah's ruling, equal in the principle of inheritance, even if they differ according to what Allah has prescribed for each of them.

quiz.question: A young man has proposed to a young woman. May he see her?
options: Yes, he sees her without seclusion, which is more likely to make affection last

quiz.question: You learned that your friend has proposed to a woman and is waiting for a reply. Do you propose to her?
options: Yes, may the best man win
No, a man does not propose to a woman his brother has proposed to

quiz.question: You are choosing a wife. What is the most important criterion the Prophet ﷺ advised?

days.title: Women One May Not Marry, and the Invalidity of Temporary Marriage
days.question: Which women may a man not marry? And what is the ruling on temporary marriage?
days.principle: It is forbidden to marry one's mothers, daughters, sisters, paternal aunts, maternal aunts, brothers' daughters, sisters' daughters, wife's mother, wife's daughter if he has consummated marriage with her mother, father's wife and son's wife. Whatever is forbidden by lineage is forbidden by nursing, and setting a time limit in the marriage contract invalidates it.

misconception.peopleSay: Temporary marriage (mut'ah) is halal as long as both parties agree.
misconception.correct: Setting a time limit in the marriage contract invalidates it, and the book points to the prohibition of mut'ah or temporary marriage with the hadith of al-Rabi' ibn Sabrah al-Juhani from his father.

days.action: Make sure you know who your mahrams through nursing are in your family (if any), because the book establishes that nursing makes forbidden what birth makes forbidden.
lesson: Among a woman's rights is the dowry (sadaq); Allah said «وآتوا النساء صدقاتهن نحلة», and the husband may not take any of it except with her willing consent. It is recommended to announce a marriage with the daff and permissible singing, and the Prophet ﷺ said that the Ansar like entertainment. Then the book lists the women one may not marry: mother, daughter, sister, paternal aunt, maternal aunt, brother's daughter, sister's daughter, wife's mother, wife's daughter if he consummated marriage with her mother, father's wife and son's wife. Also combining two sisters, or a woman and her paternal or maternal aunt. Whatever is forbidden by lineage is likewise forbidden by nursing, and the Prophet ﷺ told Aisha not to veil herself from her uncle by nursing. Then the book establishes that setting a time limit in the marriage contract invalidates it.
days.quote: In general, every woman who is forbidden by lineage, her like is forbidden by nursing.

quiz.question: As a baby, someone was nursed by a woman other than his mother. What is her daughter to him?
options: Forbidden only if he nursed a great deal
His sister by nursing, forbidden to him in marriage

quiz.question: A marriage was written as lasting only one year. What is the ruling?
options: Invalid; a time limit invalidates the marriage contract
quiz.explanation: We believe that setting a time limit in the marriage contract invalidates it.

quiz.question: A man married to a woman wants to marry her paternal aunt as well. Is that allowed?
options: No, combining a woman and her paternal aunt is haram
quiz.explanation: And combining a woman with her paternal aunt, or a woman with her maternal aunt.

days.title: The Rights of Spouses
days.question: What are the wife's rights over her husband? And what are the husband's rights over his wife?
days.principle: Marriage establishes mutual rights and duties: the husband must provide maintenance, live with his wife in kindness and lead her to obey Allah; the wife must take good care of her husband's home and children and obey him in what is not sinful.

misconception.peopleSay: Housework is not a man's job at all.
misconception.correct: Aisha was asked: What did the Prophet ﷺ do at home? She said: «كان يكون في مهنة أهله - تعني خدمة أهله - فإذا حضرت الصلاة خرج إلى الصلاة».

days.action: Help with something at home today, and remember that the Prophet ﷺ used to serve his family.
lesson: Marriage in Islam is mutual rights and duties. The husband must provide maintenance and live with his wife in kindness, and even if he dislikes something in her, Allah may place much good in it. The Prophet ﷺ said a believing man does not hate his wife entirely; if he dislikes one of her traits, he will be pleased with another, and said: the best of you are the best to their families. Aisha related that the Prophet ﷺ used to help serve his family, and when the prayer came he went out to pray. The husband must also protect his family from the Fire by leading them to obey Allah, and Allah praised Isma'il for commanding his family to pray and give zakah. The wife must take good care of her husband's home and children, and each of them is a shepherd responsible for his flock.
days.quote: And caring for the wife's Hereafter is more important, and more deserving of being asked about, than caring for her worldly life!

quiz.question: A husband says: "Housework isn't a man's job." What does the Sunnah say?
options: The Prophet ﷺ used to serve his family

quiz.question: A husband saw a trait in his wife he dislikes. What does he do?
options: Remember her good traits, and not hate her

quiz.question: Is a husband responsible only for his wife's worldly life?
options: Yes, only her food and drink
Her religion is none of his business
No, he also commands her to obey Allah and forbids her from sin
Her religion is her responsibility alone
